This vignette extends the introduction. It shows more options for the figure types, such as colours, columns, boxplots and maps. The parameters next to a figure work in Excel, as explained in the introduction and in the import vignette. The same figures can be made in R. The last sections show what is possible in R only.

1 Colours

The colours of a figure follow from the parameters colour or fill. This section shows how to choose them.

1.1 Default colours

Map a column to colour or fill and the series get the house colours. The order is the same as in the published figures. It is blue, magenta and taupe, followed by the other colours. A line chart and a column chart of the same series have the same colours. A single series is always blue.

Relevant parameters

plot_type line
title Standaardkleuren van reeksen
x jaar
y waarde
colour reeks
ylab %

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with colour-default.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_line() instead. Follow the example code in section 6.1 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_line().

1.2 Colours by position

The house palette has nine colours. Use colour_index to choose them by position. The position of a colour does not change when the default order changes.

Choose the positions yourself to keep a series on its colour, for example after you reorder the levels. Do the same when you rebuild a published figure.

Relevant parameters

plot_type line
title Gekozen kleuren op positie
x jaar
y waarde
colour reeks
colour_index 7;5;4
ylab %

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with colour-positions.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_line() instead. Follow the example code in section 6.2 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_line().

1.3 Ordered classes

Ordered classes, such as income groups, need a ramp from light to dark. The default colours are meant to be distinct, so they do not show an order. Set colour_index to continuous for the ramp. Fewer than six classes take the darkest shades. The word discrete gives the default colours again. The words qualitative, sequential, discr and blues name a palette.

Relevant parameters

plot_type col
title Geordende klassen
x jaar
y n
fill klasse
colour_index continuous
ylab aantal personen, x 1000

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with colour-ramp.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_col() instead. Follow the example code in section 6.3 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_col().

1.4 A palette with positions

colour_index takes positions or the name of a palette, not both. Use palette to choose a palette and colour_index to choose the colours in it.

Relevant parameters

plot_type col
title Posities in een palet
x jaar
y n
fill klasse
palette blues
colour_index 2;3;4;5;6
ylab aantal personen, x 1000

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with colour-palette.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_col() instead. Follow the example code in section 6.4 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_col().

1.5 One colour

A single series has one colour. line_colour sets it for a line and fill_colour for columns. A colour from outside the palette is possible as a hexadecimal code, such as #820050.

Relevant parameters

plot_type line
title Een reeks in een gekozen kleur
x jaar
y waarde
line_colour #820050
ylab %

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with colour-single.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_line() instead. Follow the example code in section 6.5 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_line().

2 Columns

The introduction shows columns with a second axis and horizontal bars. This section shows the position of the columns and the limits of the value axis.

2.1 Stacked columns

Stacked is the default position. The legend is reversed, so it reads in the same order as the stack.

Relevant parameters

plot_type col
title Toegevoegde waarde per sector
x jaar
y waarde
fill sector
ylab mld euro

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with col-stacked.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_col() instead. Follow the example code in section 6.6 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_col().

2.2 Dodged columns

With position = dodge the columns stand next to each other. The legend then follows the order of the series, so set reverse_legend to FALSE.

Relevant parameters

plot_type col
title Effect per regio en scenario
x regio
y effect
fill scenario
position dodge
reverse_legend FALSE
ylab % mutatie

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with col-dodged.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_col() instead. Follow the example code in section 6.7 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_col().

2.3 Limits and percentages

The value axis follows the data. It starts and ends where the data does. Use value_limits to set the limits yourself, such as 0 and 100 for a share. pct_axis writes the values as percentages. The axis widens when the data runs past the limits. With value_crop set to TRUE the data outside the limits is cut off, with a warning.

Relevant parameters

plot_type col
title Huishoudens zonder auto
x inkomensgroep
y share
orientation horizontal
pct_axis TRUE
value_limits 0;100
width 0.6
ylab inkomensgroep
xlab aandeel huishoudens

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with col-limits.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_col() instead. Follow the example code in section 6.8 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_col().

3 Boxplot styles

The introduction shows the default style of cpb_box() and the extended boxplot. box_style sets how a box is drawn. This section shows the other styles. All styles need the quantiles in columns, so aggregate the data first.

3.1 James style

james is the box of the old James plotter. It has no border, and a black median that sticks out. The value of the median is printed above it.

Relevant parameters

plot_type box
title Koopkracht per inkomensgroep
x groep
p5 p5
p25 p25
p50 p50
p75 p75
p95 p95
box_style james
orientation horizontal
subtitle inkomensgroep
ylab % koopkrachtmutatie

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with box-james.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_box() instead. Follow the example code in section 6.9 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_box().

3.2 Modern style

modern has light blue boxes, a thick dark blue median and the values of the quartiles below the box. The values are printed by default. Use box_labels to turn them off and label_accuracy for the rounding. james and modern draw boxes of one colour, which is set by fill_colour.

Relevant parameters

plot_type box
title Koopkracht per inkomensgroep
x groep
p5 p5
p25 p25
p50 p50
p75 p75
p95 p95
box_style modern
orientation horizontal
width 0.35
value_accuracy 0.1
subtitle inkomensgroep
ylab % koopkrachtmutatie

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with box-modern.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_box() instead. Follow the example code in section 6.10 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_box().

3.3 Dot style

dot draws no box. A dashed line runs from p5 to p95, with a light dot at each end. A bar shows the interquartile range and a dot shows the median. The optional column mean adds a diamond. A legend names each marker. Use dot_labels to rename a marker, such as p50:median in an English figure.

Relevant parameters

plot_type box
title Voorkeurstarieven erfbelasting
x erfenis
p5 p5
p25 p25
p50 p50
p75 p75
p95 p95
mean gem
box_style dot
orientation horizontal
xlab omvang erfenis
ylab voorkeurstarief (%)

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with box-dot.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_box() instead. Follow the example code in section 6.11 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_box().

3.4 Value axis on top

value_axis = top puts the value axis along the top of the figure. This works for horizontal boxes. Set the ticks with value_breaks.

Relevant parameters

plot_type box
title Koopkracht per inkomensgroep
x groep
p5 p5
p25 p25
p50 p50
p75 p75
p95 p95
box_style modern
orientation horizontal
value_axis top
value_breaks -6;-4;-2;0;2;4;6
width 0.35
subtitle statisch, verandering in %

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with box-top.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_box() instead. Follow the example code in section 6.12 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_box().

3.5 Grouped boxes

group places the categories under bold group names. All boxes share one value axis. A group with one category of the same name, such as Totaal, takes one row. fill_colour takes one colour per row. A grouped figure is taller, so this one is saved with height = 11.4.

Relevant parameters

plot_type box
title Inkomenseffecten plannen stelsel
x cat
p5 p5
p25 p25
p50 p50
p75 p75
p95 p95
group grp
box_style james
orientation horizontal
fill_colour #193c69;#87d2ff;#87d2ff;#87d2ff;#87d2ff;#87d2ff;#87d2ff;#e6006e;#e6006e;#e6006e
width 0.45
ylab verandering in 2025 (%)
height 11.4

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with box-grouped.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_box() instead. Follow the example code in section 6.13 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_box().

4 Maps

The introduction shows a map with classes. This section shows a map with numbers and a map of provinces. All maps use the boundaries that come with the package, so no other packages are needed. A map keeps its real proportions. save_cpb(preset = "map") makes it as tall as it needs. The regions are joined by their CBS code, such as GM0014, or by their name. A region without a value is grey and a region that is not found gives a warning.

4.1 Numbers on a map

A numeric value gets the sequential gradient and a colour bar. The unit goes in subtitle. A map has no value axis, so ylab does not exist. reverse turns the gradient around and na_fill sets the colour of the regions without a value.

Relevant parameters

plot_type map
title Voorbeeldindex per gemeente
region code
value index
subtitle index (Nederland = 100)

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with map-numbers.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_map() instead. Follow the example code in section 6.14 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_map().

4.2 Provinces

level = provincie draws the provinces and corop draws the COROP regions. The default level is gemeente. A text value gets the house colours. border_colour sets the colour of the borders. White gives more contrast on a map with two classes. legend = bottom puts the legend below the map and none removes it. A title wider than the map gives a warning of save_cpb(). Break it with \n, as is done here.

Relevant parameters

plot_type map
title Groei ten opzichte van hetgemiddelde
region naam
value klasse
level provincie
colour_index 2;6
border_colour white

How to reproduce this figure: copy params.csv, generate_plot.bat and the folder data with map-provinces.csv to a personal folder. Fill in the parameters above in params.csv and start the script. In R you can call cpb_map() instead. Follow the example code in section 6.15 to create the plot in R. Alternatively, the csv file can be read with read.csv() and used as input to cpb_map().

5 More possibilities in R

The figures in this section need R. Every function returns a ggplot2 object, so you can add layers and scales with +. See also the section on ggplot2 in the introduction.

5.1 A line over stacked columns

A decomposition has stacked columns and the total as a line. This is cpb_col() plus a geom_line().

componenten <- c("kapitaal/uren", "arbeidssamenstelling", "tfp")
dec <- expand_grid(
  jaar = 2000:2024,
  # reversed levels stack the first component nearest to zero
  component = factor(componenten, levels = rev(componenten))
) |>
  mutate(bijdrage = round(0.4 + 0.9 * sin(jaar * 1.3 +
                                            as.numeric(component) * 2), 1))
totaal <- dec |>
  summarise(bijdrage = sum(bijdrage), .by = jaar)

cpb_col(dec, x = jaar, y = bijdrage, fill = component,
        position = "stack", colour_index = c(2, 5, 6), width = 0.75,
        title = "Opbouw productiviteitsgroei", ylab = "%") +
  geom_line(
    data = totaal,
    mapping = aes(x = jaar, y = bijdrage, colour = "arbeidsproductiviteit"),
    linewidth = 0.55, inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_colour_cpb_manual(index = 1) +
  labs(colour = NULL) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE, order = 1),
         colour = guide_legend(order = 2)) +
  theme(legend.box = "horizontal", legend.box.just = "top")

5.2 Boxes with a fill per year

Map fill and pass a position_dodge() for two boxes per category. This works with the default style ggcpb only.

kk2 <- expand_grid(kk, jaar = factor(c(2026, 2027))) |>
  mutate(across(p5:p95, \(q) q + (jaar == "2027") * 0.8),
         groep = factor(groep, levels = rev(groepen),
                        labels = c("tot 120%\nwml", "120% wml\ntot modaal",
                                   "1 tot 1,5x\nmodaal", "1,5 tot 2x\nmodaal",
                                   "2 tot 3x\nmodaal", "boven 3x\nmodaal")))

cpb_box(kk2, x = groep,
        p5 = p5, p25 = p25, p50 = p50, p75 = p75, p95 = p95,
        fill = jaar, position = position_dodge(width = 0.6),
        colour_index = c(6, 2),
        title = "Koopkracht per jaar, 2026 en 2027",
        ylab = "% koopkrachtmutatie")

5.3 Without a wrapper

Some figures have no function in ggcpb. Build them with ggplot2 and use the same parts as the functions do, which are theme_cpb(), a colour scale and the formatters. Two house rules go with it. The unit goes in subtitle, and the title of the horizontal axis sits at the bottom right.

cpb_cut() turns the numbers into classes with Dutch labels. The scale scale_fill_cpb_d() colours the classes from light to dark. drop = FALSE keeps a class without observations in the legend, and show.legend = TRUE draws its colour.

raster <- expand.grid(groep = factor(groepen, levels = groepen),
                      jaar  = 2024:2027) |>
  mutate(mediaan = round(0.5 + 1.2 * sin(as.numeric(groep) + jaar), 1))

ggplot(raster, aes(jaar, groep,
                   fill = cpb_cut(mediaan, c(-Inf, -1, 0, 1, 2, Inf),
                                  labeller = label_pct_nl()))) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4, show.legend = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Mediane koopkracht per groep en jaar",
       subtitle = "inkomensgroep",
       x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "mediaan (%)") +
  scale_fill_cpb_d(palette = "blues", drop = FALSE) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 2)) +
  theme_cpb(grid = "none", ticks = FALSE)

5.4 Colours outside the palette

A colour that is not in the palette needs an ordinary ggplot2 scale.

cpb_line(groei, x = jaar, y = waarde, colour = reeks,
         title = "Een eigen kleurenschaal", ylab = "%") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#005faf", "#96827d", "#64504b"))

5.5 Export

save_cpb() writes a figure at the page width. It is 7.5 cm for half, 15.5 cm for full and 6.8 cm for small. The height is the report height, unless you set height. Use preset = "map" for a map and dpi for the resolution. Text sizes are absolute, so the size of the canvas is part of the design. Draw at the page width and scale only the display.

p <- cpb_col(auto, x = inkomensgroep, y = share, orientation = "horizontal")
save_cpb("koopkracht.png", p, page = "half")
save_cpb("koopkracht_breed.png", p, page = "full", height = 8 / 2.54)

6 Example code to create figures in R

The code below creates the figures above in R. It first builds the data, then draws the figure. It is the same code that made the figures in this document. Start the script with these lines.

library(conflicted)
library(ggcpb)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

options(ggcpb.style = "dutch") # style of the whole publication

6.1 Default colours

reeksen <- c("arbeidsproductiviteit", "tfp", "arbeidsvolume")
groei <- tibble(
  reeks = factor(rep(reeksen, each = 10), levels = reeksen),
  jaar  = rep(2015:2024, 3),
  waarde = c(1.2, 0.8, 1.5, 0.3, 0.9, -1.4, 3.1, 1.6, -0.2, 0.7,
             0.9, 0.2, 1.1, -0.4, 0.6, -1.9, 2.8, 1.0, -0.7, 0.3,
             0.4, 1.2, 1.8, 1.1, 0.5, -0.9, 1.6, 2.1, 1.3, 0.8)
)
cpb_line(groei, x = jaar, y = waarde, colour = reeks,
         title = "Standaardkleuren van reeksen", ylab = "%")

6.2 Colours by position

reeksen <- c("arbeidsproductiviteit", "tfp", "arbeidsvolume")
groei <- tibble(
  reeks = factor(rep(reeksen, each = 10), levels = reeksen),
  jaar  = rep(2015:2024, 3),
  waarde = c(1.2, 0.8, 1.5, 0.3, 0.9, -1.4, 3.1, 1.6, -0.2, 0.7,
             0.9, 0.2, 1.1, -0.4, 0.6, -1.9, 2.8, 1.0, -0.7, 0.3,
             0.4, 1.2, 1.8, 1.1, 0.5, -0.9, 1.6, 2.1, 1.3, 0.8)
)
cpb_line(groei, x = jaar, y = waarde, colour = reeks,
         colour_index = c(7, 5, 4),
         title = "Gekozen kleuren op positie", ylab = "%")

6.3 Ordered classes

klassen <- c("0 tot 5%", "5 tot 10%", "10 tot 20%", "20 tot 30%",
             "meer dan 30%")
intensiteit <- tibble(
  jaar   = rep(2024:2027, each = 5),
  klasse = factor(rep(klassen, 4), levels = klassen),
  n      = c(60, 120, 180, 90, 50, 70, 130, 170, 100, 60,
             80, 125, 160, 110, 75, 90, 120, 150, 120, 95)
)
cpb_col(intensiteit, x = jaar, y = n, fill = klasse,
        colour_index = "continuous",
        title = "Geordende klassen", ylab = "aantal personen, x 1000")

6.4 A palette with positions

klassen <- c("0 tot 5%", "5 tot 10%", "10 tot 20%", "20 tot 30%",
             "meer dan 30%")
intensiteit <- tibble(
  jaar   = rep(2024:2027, each = 5),
  klasse = factor(rep(klassen, 4), levels = klassen),
  n      = c(60, 120, 180, 90, 50, 70, 130, 170, 100, 60,
             80, 125, 160, 110, 75, 90, 120, 150, 120, 95)
)
cpb_col(intensiteit, x = jaar, y = n, fill = klasse,
        palette = "blues", colour_index = c(2, 3, 4, 5, 6),
        title = "Posities in een palet", ylab = "aantal personen, x 1000")

6.5 One colour

reeksen <- c("arbeidsproductiviteit", "tfp", "arbeidsvolume")
groei <- tibble(
  reeks = factor(rep(reeksen, each = 10), levels = reeksen),
  jaar  = rep(2015:2024, 3),
  waarde = c(1.2, 0.8, 1.5, 0.3, 0.9, -1.4, 3.1, 1.6, -0.2, 0.7,
             0.9, 0.2, 1.1, -0.4, 0.6, -1.9, 2.8, 1.0, -0.7, 0.3,
             0.4, 1.2, 1.8, 1.1, 0.5, -0.9, 1.6, 2.1, 1.3, 0.8)
)
tfp <- dplyr::filter(groei, reeks == "tfp")
cpb_line(tfp, x = jaar, y = waarde, line_colour = cpb_cols(3),
         title = "Een reeks in een gekozen kleur", ylab = "%")

6.6 Stacked columns

sectoren <- c("industrie", "diensten", "landbouw", "overheid")
tw <- tibble(
  jaar   = rep(2023:2027, each = 4),
  sector = factor(rep(sectoren, 5), levels = sectoren),
  waarde = c(18.2, 11.5, 24.1, 7.6, 17.4, 12.9, 22.8, 8.1, 19.6, 13.4, 21.5,
             8.8, 20.1, 12.2, 23.3, 9.4, 21.3, 14.0, 22.1, 10.2)
)
cpb_col(tw, x = jaar, y = waarde, fill = sector,
        title = "Toegevoegde waarde per sector", ylab = "mld euro")

6.7 Dodged columns

regios <- c("Noord", "Oost", "Zuid", "West")
scenarios <- c("basispad", "beleidsvariant")
scenario <- tibble(
  regio    = factor(rep(regios, each = 2), levels = regios),
  scenario = factor(rep(scenarios, 4), levels = scenarios),
  effect   = c(2.4, 3.1, -0.8, 1.2, 4.6, 5.2, 1.9, 3.3)
)
cpb_col(scenario, x = regio, y = effect, fill = scenario,
        position = "dodge", reverse_legend = FALSE,
        title = "Effect per regio en scenario", ylab = "% mutatie")

6.8 Limits and percentages

groepen <- c("boven 3x modaal", "2 tot 3x modaal", "1,5 tot 2x modaal",
             "1 tot 1,5x modaal", "120% wml tot modaal", "tot 120% wml")
auto <- tibble(
  inkomensgroep = factor(groepen, levels = groepen),
  share         = c(13, 14, 19, 26, 35, 62)
)
cpb_col(auto, x = inkomensgroep, y = share,
        orientation = "horizontal", pct_axis = TRUE,
        value_limits = c(0, 100), width = 0.6,
        title = "Huishoudens zonder auto", ylab = "inkomensgroep",
        xlab = "aandeel huishoudens")

6.9 James style

groepen <- c("boven 3x modaal", "2 tot 3x modaal", "1,5 tot 2x modaal",
             "1 tot 1,5x modaal", "120% wml tot modaal", "tot 120% wml")
kk <- tibble(
  groep = factor(groepen, levels = groepen),
  p5  = c(0.23, -1.23, -2.29, -3.35, -4.98, -6.19),
  p25 = c(2.30, 0.60, -0.21, -1.47, -2.83, -4.38),
  p50 = c(3.48, 2.01, 0.91, 0.16, -1.62, -3.06),
  p75 = c(4.92, 3.30, 2.39, 1.37, -0.27, -1.75),
  p95 = c(6.77, 5.39, 4.04, 3.37, 1.54, -0.11)
)
cpb_box(kk, x = groep,
        p5 = p5, p25 = p25, p50 = p50, p75 = p75, p95 = p95,
        box_style = "james", orientation = "horizontal",
        title = "Koopkracht per inkomensgroep", subtitle = "inkomensgroep",
        ylab = "% koopkrachtmutatie")

6.10 Modern style

groepen <- c("boven 3x modaal", "2 tot 3x modaal", "1,5 tot 2x modaal",
             "1 tot 1,5x modaal", "120% wml tot modaal", "tot 120% wml")
kk <- tibble(
  groep = factor(groepen, levels = groepen),
  p5  = c(0.23, -1.23, -2.29, -3.35, -4.98, -6.19),
  p25 = c(2.30, 0.60, -0.21, -1.47, -2.83, -4.38),
  p50 = c(3.48, 2.01, 0.91, 0.16, -1.62, -3.06),
  p75 = c(4.92, 3.30, 2.39, 1.37, -0.27, -1.75),
  p95 = c(6.77, 5.39, 4.04, 3.37, 1.54, -0.11)
)
cpb_box(kk, x = groep,
        p5 = p5, p25 = p25, p50 = p50, p75 = p75, p95 = p95,
        box_style = "modern", orientation = "horizontal", width = 0.35,
        value_accuracy = 0.1,
        title = "Koopkracht per inkomensgroep", subtitle = "inkomensgroep",
        ylab = "% koopkrachtmutatie")

6.11 Dot style

voorkeur <- tibble(
  erfenis = factor(c("1.000.000 euro", "100.000 euro", "10.000 euro"),
                   levels = c("1.000.000 euro", "100.000 euro",
                              "10.000 euro")),
  p5  = c(0, 0, 0),
  p25 = c(10, 4, 0),
  p50 = c(25, 11, 4),
  p75 = c(45, 26, 12),
  p95 = c(75, 54, 47),
  gem = c(30, 19, 11)
)
cpb_box(voorkeur, x = erfenis,
        p5 = p5, p25 = p25, p50 = p50, p75 = p75, p95 = p95, mean = gem,
        box_style = "dot", orientation = "horizontal",
        title = "Voorkeurstarieven erfbelasting", xlab = "omvang erfenis",
        ylab = "voorkeurstarief (%)")

6.12 Value axis on top

groepen <- c("boven 3x modaal", "2 tot 3x modaal", "1,5 tot 2x modaal",
             "1 tot 1,5x modaal", "120% wml tot modaal", "tot 120% wml")
kk <- tibble(
  groep = factor(groepen, levels = groepen),
  p5  = c(0.23, -1.23, -2.29, -3.35, -4.98, -6.19),
  p25 = c(2.30, 0.60, -0.21, -1.47, -2.83, -4.38),
  p50 = c(3.48, 2.01, 0.91, 0.16, -1.62, -3.06),
  p75 = c(4.92, 3.30, 2.39, 1.37, -0.27, -1.75),
  p95 = c(6.77, 5.39, 4.04, 3.37, 1.54, -0.11)
)
cpb_box(kk, x = groep,
        p5 = p5, p25 = p25, p50 = p50, p75 = p75, p95 = p95,
        box_style = "modern", orientation = "horizontal",
        value_axis = "top", value_breaks = seq(-6, 6, 2), width = 0.35,
        title = "Koopkracht per inkomensgroep",
        subtitle = "statisch, verandering in %")

6.13 Grouped boxes

inkomen <- c("tot 120% wml", "120% wml tot modaal", "1 tot 1,5x modaal",
             "1,5 tot 2x modaal", "2 tot 3x modaal", "boven 3x modaal")
bron <- c("Werkenden", "Uitkeringsgerechtigden", "Gepensioneerden")
categorieen <- c("Totaal", inkomen, bron)
ink <- tibble(
  cat = factor(categorieen, levels = categorieen),
  grp = factor(rep(c("Totaal", "Inkomensgroepen", "Inkomensbron"),
                   c(1, 6, 3)),
               levels = c("Totaal", "Inkomensgroepen", "Inkomensbron")),
  p50 = c(0.09, 0.02, 0.07, 0.07, 0.06, 0.04, 0.05, 0.09, 0.04, 0.05)
) |>
  mutate(p25 = p50 - 0.08, p75 = p50 + 0.07,
         p5 = p25 - 0.35, p95 = p75 + 0.35)
cpb_box(ink, x = cat, p5 = p5, p25 = p25, p50 = p50, p75 = p75, p95 = p95,
        group = grp, box_style = "james", orientation = "horizontal",
        fill_colour = c("#193c69", rep("#87d2ff", 6), rep("#e6006e", 3)),
        width = 0.45, title = "Inkomenseffecten plannen stelsel",
        ylab = "verandering in 2025 (%)")

6.14 Numbers on a map

codes <- unique(cpb_nl_geo("gemeente")$code)
gemeenten_ct <- tibble(
  code  = codes,
  index = round(100 + 12 * sin(seq_along(codes) / 9), 1)
)
cpb_map(gemeenten_ct, region = code, value = index,
        title = "Voorbeeldindex per gemeente",
        subtitle = "index (Nederland = 100)")

6.15 Provinces

namen <- unique(cpb_nl_geo("provincie")$name)
provincies <- tibble(
  naam   = namen,
  klasse = factor(rep(c("onder gemiddeld", "boven gemiddeld"), 6),
                  levels = c("onder gemiddeld", "boven gemiddeld"))
)
cpb_map(provincies, region = naam, value = klasse, level = "provincie",
        colour_index = c(2, 6), border_colour = "white",
        title = "Groei ten opzichte van het\nlandelijk gemiddelde")
